instruction:
You are interviewing a shop about a job they already do, until the procedure is unambiguous enough that two different technicians working alone would produce the same record. Ask about ONE thing per turn, in their language, never in the vocabulary of forms. Compile only when nothing material is still unstated: every step has a reason someone would accept, every field has an acceptance rule that can actually be applied to what comes back, and a bound that came from the shop rather than from you. Inventing a tolerance is the one thing you must never do — a figure nobody stated must not appear in what you compile. A shop that does not know one will not know it when asked again: take the first 'I don't know' as final, keep it in unresolved if it matters, and move on. Your turns are few. Spend them on the figures that decide whether the job passed, never on detail beneath them.

Return JSON with these fields:
- mode (one of ask | compile, required): ask while anything material is unstated. compile once the procedure would run unambiguously.
- question (string, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is ask. One question about one thing, phrased for a mechanic, not a form designer. Never a list, never a preamble, never a restatement of what they just told you, and never one they have already said they cannot answer.
- asks_about (one of scope | sequence | tolerance | evidence | failure | authority | parts | safety, null when it does not apply): Which class of unknown this question closes. Required when mode is ask.
- unresolved (array, required): Everything you still do not know that would change the compiled procedure. Complete every turn, not only what you just asked about. Empty is the only condition under which you may compile.
- understanding (string, required): What you now believe the job is, in two sentences. Written every turn so the shop can correct you early rather than at the end.
- draft (object, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is compile. The procedure as it would run tomorrow.

output.understanding: The job is a front brake pad service and safety check to prepare rental motorcycles for gravel riding. The technician inspects the disc for contamination, measures the front pads (replacing them if under 2 mm), photographs the installed pads, torques the caliper to 30 Nm, and beds them in with 20 gentle stops.

draft.title: Front Brake Pad Service
disqualifiers: Fork oil or brake fluid on the disc
releases: Rental safety clearance for front brakes

steps.title: Inspect Disc for Contamination
steps.explanation: Fork oil or brake fluid on the disc will contaminate the pads and cause brake failure.

fields.prompt: Check the brake disc for any signs of fork oil or brake fluid.
fields.guidance: Any presence of oil or fluid on the disc is an immediate safety failure.

steps.title: Measure Pad Thickness
steps.explanation: Pads worn below 2 mm do not have enough friction material to safely last another rental.

fields.prompt: Enter the thickness of the thinnest front brake pad.
fields.guidance: Pads must be at least 2 mm thick to pass. If they are thinner, they must be replaced.

steps.title: Install and Photograph Pads
steps.explanation: Verifies that the pads are correctly seated in the caliper before the wheel goes back on.

fields.prompt: Take a photo of the pads sitting in the caliper before the wheel goes back on.
fields.acceptance_description: Both brake pads correctly seated in the caliper.
fields.guidance: Ensure the photo clearly shows the pads installed in the caliper before reassembling.

steps.title: Torque Caliper Bolts
steps.explanation: Caliper bolts must be torqued to specification to prevent them from backing out under braking forces.

fields.prompt: Torque the caliper bolts to 30 Nm.
fields.guidance: Use a torque wrench to tighten the caliper bolts to exactly 30 Nm.

steps.title: Bed In Pads
steps.explanation: Bedding in the pads ensures full contact and proper stopping power before the customer rides.

fields.prompt: Perform 20 gentle stops down the lane to bed in the pads.
fields.guidance: Bed in the pads by performing 20 gentle stops down the lane to ensure proper stopping power.

steps.title: Technician Sign-off
steps.explanation: The technician performing the work must sign off to attest that the front brakes are safe for rental.

fields.prompt: Sign to certify that the front brakes have been serviced and are safe for rental.
fields.guidance: Your signature certifies that the front brake pads are safe and the caliper is torqued.
